name: GetYourGuide
summary: The backend interview gives you a small Spring Boot codebase with planted problems. You get the code shortly before a live round where you pair on it, fix it and answer questions about it.
confidence: Confirmed = from the company's prep document. Reported = candidate reports (Glassdoor, April 2026). Likely = one candidate's prep notes, not independently confirmed.

process.format: About 30 minutes with a recruiter: CV screen, the position and why GetYourGuide. Generic questions. One candidate says the recruiter forgot to send the coding test for five days until they followed up by email.

HackerRank assessment with about 7 days to finish. Reported tasks: an event registration service with add-event, register, cancel and list-registrations operations (one review describes a 90-minute automated tech screen), and a later task to change a query so it does not return rows with duplicate values. One candidate says the tests expect thorough test cases. Other reports: one LeetCode-medium task in about 1 hour, and a string manipulation task. One candidate found it hard but passed.
The repository link arrives about 24 hours before the technical interview, and you must set it up beforehand. It is public on GetYourGuide's GitHub page. Java and Spring Boot with a few endpoints.

60 minutes with one or two engineers: about 5 minutes of intro, 50 minutes of live pair programming on the codebase, and 5 minutes of Q&A. Java and Spring Boot. The prep document says the code is 'a simple project that wasn't made with best practices in mind'. Reported tasks: fix an endpoint that throws a NullPointerException or returns 500, modify endpoints, write tests, solve a task with maps, change a query so it returns no rows with a duplicate value in column1, and answer SQL, indexing and Streams questions. Reports differ: some ran 45 minutes, and one candidate failed on the SQL part.

AI tools such as Copilot or Claude Code are allowed. Expect to explain which tool you chose for which task and why. Reported: they want prompts that are specific, not generic, and tests for everything the AI changes. One candidate advises using AI only to show a smart prompt strategy. Reported questions: AI use at work, tasks where engineers should not use AI, and mentoring a colleague on AI.
About 1 hour with an engineering manager. Basic behavioral questions. Reported by one candidate (Zurich, July 2025).

Reports mention stack ranking: several candidates pass the technical round and the team picks one. Feedback can be vague. One candidate had the next technical round cancelled a day before because the position was filled. One candidate was not invited further after the pairing round. Timelines range from 6 days to 3 weeks.

study_plan.how: Build a small Spring Boot app with JPA and PostgreSQL or H2. Add an entity with a lazy relation.
Load 100 parents with lazy children and count the queries. Fix it with a fetch join or entity graph, then count again.
Write controller, service and repository layers. Map each exception to a status code with @RestControllerAdvice. No catch-all handler.
Practise the @Data pitfalls, IDENTITY vs AUTO, and wrapper vs primitive for nullable columns.
Write one @WebMvcTest, one @DataJpaTest and one @SpringBootTest. Test through MockMvc. Delete any mock nothing uses.
Solve the event registration challenge in 60 minutes, with tests. Then do a query-deduplication task the same way.
Use your own project with planted bugs, or write one. Practise narrating a 50-minute fix out loud: find, explain, change, test.
List which tool you would use for which task and why. Be ready to say what you checked in its output.

topics.name: Layering
topics.what: What each layer owns: controllers handle HTTP, services hold business rules, repositories do data access. Why a service should not depend on a controller.

topics.name: JPA and Hibernate
topics.what: N+1 queries and fetch joins, read-only transactions, lazy loading outside a transaction, and how the entity mapping choices affect behaviour.

topics.name: Entities
topics.what: Why Lombok @Data is risky on JPA entities, id generation strategies, primitive vs wrapper types for nullable columns, and what @NotFound does.

topics.name: Queries
topics.what: JPQL vs native SQL, constructor expressions in JPQL, aggregate queries with a typed result, and case-insensitive search.

topics.name: Errors and HTTP
topics.what: @RestController vs @Controller, exception handlers mapped to the right status codes, and why a catch-all handler is a problem.

topics.name: Java
topics.what: Streams and lambdas, side effects in forEach, checked exceptions inside lambdas, and null handling in more than one place.

topics.name: Testing
topics.what: Spring test slices (@WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest, @SpringBootTest), MockMvc vs calling controller methods directly, and why dead mocks mislead reviewers.

topics.name: AI in the round
topics.what: Using an AI tool well: say what you asked it, check the output, and explain the result in your own words.

topics.name: Production query tuning
topics.what: How to investigate a slow query in production: measure first, read the execution plan, check indexes and row counts, then fix and re-measure.

questions.q: The same mapping code appears in three service methods. How do you remove the duplication, and what is wrong with using forEach to add to a list?
questions.a: Extract one mapping function and use stream().map(). forEach with an external list hides the result and invites side effects. Each mapped value should be returned, not added to a shared list.

questions.q: Why should a service not depend on a controller?
questions.a: The dependency runs the wrong way. Controllers are the HTTP edge and depend on services. A service that calls a controller couples business logic to the web layer and creates cycles.

questions.q: Why should a controller not use EntityManager directly?
questions.a: Data access belongs in the repository layer. A controller that writes queries skips the rules and transactions the repository and service provide, and it is harder to test.

questions.q: Lookup by id loads every row with findAll() and then filters in Java. What happens with ten million rows?
questions.a: All rows are loaded into memory, which is slow and can exhaust the heap. Query by id with findById, or add a WHERE clause in JPQL.

questions.q: A search method fills one list and returns another empty list. What does it return?
questions.a: Always an empty list. Items are added to one list but the other is returned. It is a copy-paste bug and is easy to miss in review.

questions.q: How many queries does it take to list 100 activities when each activity lazily loads its supplier?
questions.a: 101: one query for the activities and one per supplier (N+1). Fix it with a fetch join, for example LEFT JOIN FETCH a.supplier, or an entity graph.

questions.q: Why add @Transactional(readOnly = true) to read methods?
questions.a: Hibernate skips dirty checking for read-only transactions, which saves work. Some setups also route read-only transactions to a replica. It is a hint, not a database-level lock.

questions.q: Why can't a checked exception be thrown inside a lambda in a stream?
questions.a: Standard functional interfaces such as Function don't declare checked exceptions, so the compiler rejects the throw. Use a RuntimeException subclass, or catch and wrap the checked exception inside the lambda.

questions.q: What is the difference between @Controller and @RestController?
questions.a: @Controller treats a return value as a view name unless the method has @ResponseBody. @RestController adds @ResponseBody to every method, so return values are written as the response body.

questions.q: What is wrong with one @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) for the whole app?
questions.a: Every error becomes a 500, including a not-found case that should return 404. Add a handler per exception type with the right status code.

questions.q: A search finds nothing. What should it return, and why is a fallback to all suppliers wrong?
questions.a: An empty result with 200, because no match is a valid answer. Returning everything when nothing matches shows the wrong data. Use a case-insensitive query, for example LOWER(...) LIKE, for the match itself.

questions.q: Why is @Data dangerous on a JPA entity?
questions.a: Its generated equals, hashCode and toString read every field, including lazy relations and back-references. That can trigger LazyInitializationException, or a StackOverflowError when parent and child print each other. Exclude relations and use the id for equality.

questions.q: What does @NotFound(action = IGNORE) do when the referenced row is missing?
questions.a: Hibernate silently sets the association to null instead of throwing. Callers must handle null, and bad data stays hidden.

questions.q: What is the difference between GenerationType.AUTO and IDENTITY?
questions.a: IDENTITY uses the database's auto-increment column. AUTO lets the provider pick, which can mean a sequence or a table, depending on the dialect. Choose the strategy on purpose.

questions.q: Why use Double rather than double in an entity?
questions.a: A wrapper type can be null, which matches a nullable database column. A primitive is always set, so a null column cannot be mapped.

questions.q: What can go wrong with a JPQL constructor expression that builds a DTO?
questions.a: JPQL calls the constructor by position. A missing all-args constructor fails, and a field order that differs from the select list gives wrong values with no error. Keep the order in step and put the DTO in the dto package.

questions.q: A statistics method uses SELECT * into List<Object[]>. What is wrong?
questions.a: It doesn't compute statistics, it returns raw rows. Object[] is not type-safe. Use COUNT, AVG and SUM with GROUP BY, mapped to a typed DTO.

questions.q: What is the difference between @WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest and @SpringBootTest?
questions.a: @WebMvcTest loads only the web layer with mocked services. @DataJpaTest loads only persistence. @SpringBootTest loads the full context, which is slower and closer to production.

questions.q: Why is calling controller methods directly in a test weak?
questions.a: It skips HTTP: no status codes, no JSON serialisation, no filters or validation. Use MockMvc.perform(get(...)) to test through the request path.

questions.q: Why add @AutoConfigureTestDatabase(replace = NONE) to a @DataJpaTest?
questions.a: Without it, Spring swaps your configured datasource for an embedded one, so the project's migrations and database settings may not run in the test.

questions.q: When would you not use AI in the job?
questions.a: When the task measures your own understanding, such as a design you will own, a security review, or explaining a production incident. Use AI to speed up known work, and check its output.

questions.q: What is your experience with using AI at work?
questions.a: Name the tools, the tasks you give them, and one concrete result. Say what you check in the output, such as tests and review, and where it failed you.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you mentored a colleague on using AI.
questions.a: Use one real story: the colleague's problem, what you showed (specific prompts, giving context, asking for tests, reviewing the output), and how their work changed. Avoid a generic tips list.

questions.q: You are asked to use AI to improve a controller class. What do you prompt?
questions.a: Be specific: state the problem, the layer rules, the behaviour to keep, and ask for tests with the change. Then read the diff, run the tests, and explain it in your own words. A generic 'improve this code' prompt shows little.

questions.q: An endpoint throws a NullPointerException, or returns 500. How do you find and fix it?
questions.a: Reproduce the call, read the stack trace to the exact line, and find which value is null and why. Fix the cause, such as a missing check, a bad mapping or an Optional ignored, not a catch-all. Add a test that fails before the fix, and return the right status, such as 404 when nothing is found.

questions.q: A query is slow in production. How do you investigate, troubleshoot and fix it?
questions.a: Find the query from slow-query logs or monitoring. Run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) and look for full scans, bad join order and row estimates that are far off. Check indexes, N+1 patterns, missing WHERE clauses and stale statistics. Change one thing, such as an index or a rewritten query, test on production-like data, and measure again.

questions.q: Change a query so it does not return rows with a duplicate value in column1.
questions.a: Clarify which row to keep per value. Use GROUP BY column1 with aggregates, or ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY column1 ORDER BY ...) and keep row 1. Plain DISTINCT removes only fully identical rows, so it is usually not enough.

questions.q: A task needs a Map. How do you solve it, for example grouping or counting?
questions.a: Use computeIfAbsent for grouping, merge or getOrDefault for counting, or Collectors.groupingBy and counting with streams. Pick HashMap for lookup, LinkedHashMap for insertion order and TreeMap for sorted keys.

questions.q: HackerRank: build an event registration system with addEvent(eventId, eventType, capacity, requirements), registerParticipant(eventId, participantId, email, skillLevel), cancelRegistration(eventId, participantId) and findRegisteredEvents(participantId).
questions.a: Keep a Map<eventId, Event> and a Map<participantId, Set<eventId>> for fast lookup. Register must reject an unknown event, a full event, a duplicate registration and a skill level below the requirements. Cancel removes from both maps. Write tests for each rejection and for cancel then re-register.

questions.q: Basic questions on Streams, lambdas, Optional, HashSet and Maps.
questions.a: Know map, filter and collect; Optional.map and orElseThrow instead of get; HashSet for uniqueness with O(1) lookup and the equals and hashCode contract; and HashMap internals.

questions.q: What do you know about database indexing and query performance?
questions.a: An index speeds up reads on the columns you filter, join or sort on, and costs writes and space. Know B-tree indexes, composite column order, covering indexes, and when the planner ignores an index, such as a function on the column.
